**Note:** No URL was provided in the article text, so publication date cannot be verified via fetch. Based on internal context clues (references to 2022 heatwave, post-2022 taskforce, derailments described as recent), the article was likely published in **late summer 2022**.

---

**Published online:**
~ August–September 2022 (exact date not verifiable; inferred from internal references)

**Geographic focus:**
Europe > United Kingdom (England: East Sussex, Essex; broader GB rail network)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation — YES
T2. Forward-looking immediate — YES
T3. Long-term development — YES

**Synopsis:**
Britain's rail network is struggling under extreme summer heat, with track buckling, soil shrinkage under embankments, and two derailments linked to the 2022 heatwave. The article explains thermal rail physics, current mitigation measures (pre-stressing, white paint, slab track), their limitations, and the structural gap between UK rail engineering tolerances and increasingly hot summers driven by climate change. Forward-looking elements include debate over raising stress-free temperatures, better sensor data automation, and climate adaptation needs.
